cases.rationale: Direct interoperable public waterway GIS/database and information-publication governance across the named agencies is an independent technology/data-system mechanism under the existing rule. Include only this qualified whole choice; section7 prevents interpreting information access as expanded physical access.
cases.strongest_counterevidence: Recreation/fisheries management rather than transport construction; no new access right or capital project and duties have feasibility/practicability qualifications.

cases.rationale: This exact two-section change only extends an existing discretionary biological-control/restoration grant authorization and makes a technical comma correction. The baseline Maryland research reference is counterevidence but the bill adds no independent technology-development or research-governance mechanism and no operative transportation/infrastructure system change. This is a proposed case decision, not a rule excluding environmental, grant, restoration or research work.
cases.strongest_counterevidence: Wetland/agricultural restoration can affect physical landscapes and baseline Maryland activities include research; those facts require reading, but neither alone supplies the whole exact renewal an independent mechanism under this domain rule.

cases.rationale: The whole candidate is grounded, but public-site boundary feasibility planning and historic-park administration point in different directions under the existing infrastructure governance rule. Route this exact eligibility choice for review with its full study scope and conditional deadline rather than inventing a rule or treating a study as construction. No eligibility decision is applied.
cases.strongest_counterevidence: A mandatory feasibility/suitability study of named public park facilities can govern future public-site footprint planning. Conversely this measure only redesignates an existing historic park and studies possible additions, without construction, acquisition or actual boundary change.

cases.rationale: Statutory governance of an identified equipment/tagging, data-processing and scientific evaluation program, with specified collaboration/data recipients and authorization, is an independent technology/research-governance mechanism in this whole choice. The rationale rests on those operative duties, not fisheries keywords, legislative findings or an assumed external plan.
cases.strongest_counterevidence: Primarily fisheries conservation/management, no transportation construction, optional purchases and no realized deployment. Its statutory program and mandatory collaboration/data availability supply the narrower research-governance basis.

cases.rationale: The whole mixed package governs named watershed restoration/monitoring programs, grant implementation and cost shares, testing-technology guidance and contamination-source data, with defined authorizations/conditions. Those operative water-system monitoring and technical-program mechanisms supply an independent case basis; the full foreign-fund restriction and GAO component remain part of the choice. No all-environmental-law inclusion rule or universal construction claim follows.
cases.strongest_counterevidence: Broad conservation/public-health and grant administration, including an oversight report and foreign-fund conditions; several programs restrict certain water-infrastructure assistance and authorize rather than appropriate funds. The mixed whole cannot be reduced to a favorable restoration component.
